references.text: The Lord warns that the sky will become like iron and the earth like bronze, and that the land will not yield its produce as punishment for disobedience.
A parallel curse where the sky becomes like bronze and the earth like iron, without rain, as a consequence of breaking the covenant.
Solomon prays that God will hear the people's prayer when the sky is shut up and there is no rain because of sin.
Elijah prophesies that neither dew nor rain shall come upon Israel, fulfilling the warning in Deuteronomy.
Jeremiah describes how the people's sins have withheld the rain and prevented the blessings of the harvest.
Amos tells how God withheld rain from Israel as punishment and a call to repentance.
Haggai describes how the sky held back dew and the land its produce because of the people's neglect.
James refers to Elijah, who prayed and the sky was shut for three years and six months, and then opened again.
The two witnesses have power to shut the sky so that no rain falls, echoing God's judgment described in Deuteronomy.
